topics.title: Circle Properties
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: Identify arc, chord, sector and segment. (k)
Relate angles made by an arc at the circumference and centre. (u)
Determine the tangent, chord and angle properties of the circle. (u)
Determine and uses the properties of a cyclic quadrilateral. (u, s)
Find the length of the common chord for two intersecting circles. (u, s)
Calculate the area of sectors and segments. (u, s, v/a)

body.text: Building on Senior 2's Circle topic: an arc is part of the circumference; a chord is a straight line joining two points on the circle; a sector is the pie-slice region between two radii and an arc; a segment is the region between a chord and an arc.

Key circle theorems: the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc. The angle in a semicircle is always 90°. A tangent to a circle is always perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of contact. Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral (a four-sided shape with all corners on the circle) always add up to 180°.

body.expr: angle at centre = 2 x angle at circumference (same arc);   opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°

body.text: The area of a sector with angle θ (in degrees) and radius r is a fraction of the whole circle's area: (θ/360) x πr^2. A sector with radius 6 cm and angle 60° has area (60/360) x π x 6^2 = (1/6) x π x 36 = 6π ≈ 18.85 cm^2.
